title: Generating Structural Targets
author: Courtney Comrie
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7xthpnn
materials: First import your T2 Data Type: ImportBrukerAnatomical

steps.title: Import anatomical data
steps.instruction: In a terminal, type `ImportBrukerAnatomical` to launch the import utility; follow the prompts for input (-i), output (-o), and configuration (-c) options.

steps.title: Extract single T2 volume
steps.instruction: Use the ExtractImage command with the path to your T2 NIfTI file and specify the desired volume index, e.g., `ExtractImage -i /directory_name/file_name_T2.nii -v 3`. Replace `3` with the appropriate volume number for your data.

steps.title: Rigidly register extracted image
steps.instruction: After extraction, carry out a rigid registration of the extracted T2 image to align it with the reference space (method as defined in your processing pipeline).

steps.title: Open MIPAV
steps.instruction: In a terminal, run `/rsgrps/hutchinsone/Programming/mipav/mipav`; the MIPAV graphical interface should open automatically.

steps.title: Change to T2 data directory
steps.instruction: In the terminal, `cd` to the directory that contains the raw T2 data files.

steps.title: View T2 image
steps.instruction: Open the extracted T2 image using MRtrix, ITK‑SNAP, or MIPAV and select the echo that best matches the DTI data.

substeps.instruction: ITK‑SNAP: `cd /rsgrps/hutchinsone/Singularity_Containers`; `module load singularity`; `singularity run nklab-neurotools-v0.4.sif itksnap`.

steps.title: Midsagittal line alignment
steps.instruction: If the T2 image appears tilted, use MIPAV menu: Algorithms → Brain tools → Midsagittal line alignment.

steps.title: Open extracted image
steps.instruction: In MIPAV, select File → Open image (A), navigate to the directory with your extracted image, and open it.

steps.title: Correct display issues
steps.instruction: Check the slice/echelon sliders; if moving the top bar darkens the image instead of scrolling through slices, go to Utilities → 4D volume tools → “Swap dims 3 4” to fix the dimension order. Use the magnifying tool (Shift‑click) to zoom into the image as needed.
